ctx.x: Were there certain parts of the world where, let’s say the melodic contributions came from? We’ve been talking mostly about rhythm. What about the melody and the form?

Without a doubt much of the information that we have in the thing we call jazz comes from European melodicism. It comes from the chromatic, you know chromatic harmony. So in some ways this is funny that you said that because I was just listening to “Isfahan” © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

and I was just again — I was listening to “Isfahan” and “Warm Valley” and I was thinking about one of the greatest gifts of music is Duke Ellington’s sense of melodicism. Just the pacing and the outlaying of a Duke Ellington melody, to me, is as elegant as anything that Beethoven wrote and I’m a classically trained musician. My degrees are in classical music. But when I listen to Duke Ellington I can’t help but think this is classical music. It’s — you don’t have to dress it up. It’s already arrived fully formed…
